DATE: 13 Mar 2025
COUNTRY: Gabon
FUNCTION: Drilling
CAUSE: Caught in, under or between (excl. dropped objects)
ACTIVITY: Transport - Land
PRIMARY LIFE-SAVING RULE: Driving
SECONARY LIFE-SAVING RULE: Line of fire
NARRATIVE:
On Thursday March 13th, 2025, the crew change bus had a road accident. It was 18h30 and after a heavy rain at the
time of the incident.
The bus driver was driving too close to the road edge to avoid potholes of the road section. While doing so a part of
the road edge collapsed under the right front bus tire making the bus end its trajectory on the pipelines on the side
of the road with 28 pax on board.
Immediate action:
• An alcohol test was performed (negative).
• The TAG removed.
• Rearranged work because of restricted mobility due to ankle sprain.
WHAT WENT WRONG:
Road accident: Bus swerved to avoid potholes and crashed ending up on its side. During emergency exit, one
passenger twisted his ankle badly and ended with a lost injury.
CORRECTIVE ACTIONS AND RECOMMENDATIONS:
The bus had design flaws, and all buses of this type were completely removed from our bus fleet. In addition, the
procedure for driving on our laterite roads was reviewed.
CAUSAL FACTORS:
PEOPLE (ACTS): Following Procedures: Improper position (in the line of fire)
PEOPLE (ACTS): Following Procedures: Work or motion at improper speed
PROCESS (CONDITIONS): Work Place Hazards: Inadequate surfaces, floors, walkways or roads
PROCESS (CONDITIONS): Work Place Hazards: Storms or acts of nature
PROCESS (CONDITIONS): Organizational: Inadequate hazard identification or risk assessment

original_report:
DATE: 01 May 2025
COUNTRY: Gabon
FUNCTION: Drilling
CAUSE: Struck by (not dropped object)
ACTIVITY: Lifting, crane, rigging, deck operations
PRIMARY LIFE-SAVING RULE: Safe mechanical lifting
SECONARY LIFE-SAVING RULE: Line of fire
NARRATIVE:
At around 4am on 1st of May, the two men on the crane were assigned to a new location. The operation involved
depositing the counterweights. Following a counter-order from the supervisor, they had to carry out a final lift
before going on to the new location. The spider chains were replaced on the counterweights. As the chains are
lifted, one of the hooks gets caught in the guide of the counterweight. When the chains come off, they have a spring
effect. The banksman can't reasonably control three of them and the fourth spins around him with his back lower.
The spider chain hit the banksman at the back. The IP received pain killer treatment before transferring to hospital
by chopper. The IP suffered a permanent impairment injury.
WHAT WENT WRONG:
The banksman was hit by one of the four hooks on the spider chain.
CORRECTIVE ACTIONS AND RECOMMENDATIONS:
• Poor work planning.
• Inadequate communication between workers.
• Inadequate execution of the operation.
• Failure to follow lifting procedures, resulting in risks becoming normalized.
CAUSAL FACTORS:
PEOPLE (ACTS): Following Procedures: Improper position (in the line of fire)
PEOPLE (ACTS): Following Procedures: Improper lifting or loading
PEOPLE (ACTS): Inattention/Lack of Awareness: Improper decision making or lack of judgment
PROCESS (CONDITIONS): Organizational: Inadequate hazard identification or risk assessment

original_report:
DATE: 18 Aug 2025
COUNTRY: Gabon
FUNCTION: Drilling
CAUSE: Struck by (not dropped object)
ACTIVITY: Lifting, crane, rigging, deck operations
PRIMARY LIFE-SAVING RULE: Line of fire
SECONARY LIFE-SAVING RULE: Work authorization
NARRATIVE:
On 18 August 2025, a team was installing a 6-inch pipe over a 35-metre section between two lines. This pipe was
also to be used during WO operations. During the operation, the team separated a 6-inch pipe from a 2-inch pipe,
both of which had previously been tied together with cords. During the lifting phase, the cords were gradually cut
to separate the two pipes. When the third cord was cut, the tension accumulated in the 6-inch pipe, which was
bent at the time, was suddenly released. The pipe rebounded and struck an operator's right leg between the ankle
and knee, causing an open fracture. The supervisor was immediately informed, the control room was alerted, and
emergency procedures were quickly implemented.
WHAT WENT WRONG:
PI: Right leg open fracture of staff during the connection operation, while lifting a 6-inch pipe and a 2-inch pipe,
both of which had previously been tied together with ropes on the 18th August 2025.
CORRECTIVE ACTIONS AND RECOMMENDATIONS:
All work performed requires a dedicated method statement/JHA. The JHA and PTW are updated for all job
applicants. Improve the behaviour of the authorities responsible for stopping work at all subcontractors. Review the
management of the contract.
CAUSAL FACTORS:
PEOPLE (ACTS): Following Procedures: Improper position (in the line of fire)
PEOPLE (ACTS): Use of Tools, Equipment, Materials and Products: Improper use/position of tools/equipment/
materials/products
PEOPLE (ACTS): Inattention/Lack of Awareness: Improper decision making or lack of judgment

original_report:
DATE: 19 Jan 2025
COUNTRY: Gabon
FUNCTION: Construction
CAUSE: Explosion, fire or burns
ACTIVITY: Maintenance, inspection, testing
PRIMARY LIFE-SAVING RULE: Work authorization
SECONARY LIFE-SAVING RULE: Bypassing safety controls
NARRATIVE:
On January 19, 2025, during restart attempts of the HP-A Gas Compressor following corrective maintenance,
an unusually loud noise was heard from the exhaust. Seconds later, the fire alarm was triggered, and it was
observed that the exhaust structure had fallen off. Technicians in the vicinity immediately pressed the compressor’s
emergency stop button and evacuated the facility. Simultaneously, the emergency response team was activated, and
the on-scene commander initiated a full facility shutdown using a manual call point near the compressor building.
Once the source of the loud noise was confirmed to be the HP-A compressor, with the exhaust lying on the ground,
the area was cordoned off, and an investigation was launched. The compressor was manually shut down, and the
ESD-1 emergency stop was activated.
WHAT WENT WRONG:
During the starting of gas lift compressor (HP-A), the exhaust pipe of the engine driving the reciprocating
compressor broke and fell off after several attempts to start it, subsequently activating the fire alarm.
CORRECTIVE ACTIONS AND RECOMMENDATIONS:
The crew was not very familiar with the model of engine and didn't know how to react after 1 or 2 attempts to
restart.
The operating manual was in English not fully understood by the maintenance team.
CAUSAL FACTORS:
PEOPLE (ACTS): Following Procedures: Deviation unintentional (by individual or group)
PEOPLE (ACTS): Use of Protective Methods: Failure to warn of hazard
PEOPLE (ACTS): Inattention/Lack of Awareness: Improper decision making or lack of judgment
PROCESS (CONDITIONS): Organizational: Inadequate hazard identification or risk assessment

original_report:
DATE: 25 Mar 2025
COUNTRY: Ghana
FUNCTION: Unspecified
CAUSE: Dropped objects
ACTIVITY: Office, warehouse, accommodation, catering
PRIMARY LIFE-SAVING RULE: Line of fire
NARRATIVE:
During a heavy rainstorm, two aluminium composite panels (component of the external cladding material for the
Office building) dislodged and dropped. The two (2) panels, each weighing 9.8kgs and measuring 1.11x1.49ms,
dropped from about a height of 22.35 meters. The fallen panels were found Infront of the South Wing Power room,
and the affected area was promptly cordoned off to prevent further hazards. Additionally, multiple panels were
observed hanging loosely, posing a potential safety risk to occupants and visitors.
WHAT WENT WRONG:
1. Aluminium composite panels not airtight. - Previous investigations revealed that no consideration was given
to the potential for panels falling during design and installation. Furthermore, subsequent structural integrity
assessments did not clearly establish the mode of failure and effective mitigation measures to prevent recurrence.
Additionally, in cases where potentially falling aluminium composite panels have been reported, remedial actions to
remove and reinstall such panels are not promptly executed, despite the high potential impact of a dropped panel.
2. Corrective action process not effectively implemented. - There has been recurring near misses involving dropped
Aluminium Composite Panels in 2016, 2017, 2018, and 2024. However, corrective actions, such as implementing
monthly and quarterly drop inspections, have not been sustained.
Furthermore, planned preventive maintenance and other assurance activities that were instituted have not been
consistently followed and remain areas requiring improvement. For instance, the annual integrity assessment for
2023 and 2024 were not conducted as planned.
CORRECTIVE ACTIONS AND RECOMMENDATIONS:
1. Conduct an integrity inspection and assessment of the external of the entire building to identify any areas of loose
cladding and fix them immediately to prevent any potential recurrence of the incident in the short term.
2. Re-institute the conduct of the annual inspection programme of the entire exterior of the building's facade to
identify any areas of loose cladding and fix them immediately to prevent any potential dropped objects.
CAUSAL FACTORS:
PEOPLE (ACTS): Following Procedures: Improper position (in the line of fire)
PEOPLE (ACTS): Use of Protective Methods: Equipment or materials not secured

original_report:
DATE: 26 Jul 2025
COUNTRY: Nigeria
FUNCTION: Drilling
CAUSE: Struck by (not dropped object)
ACTIVITY: Lifting, crane, rigging, deck operations
PRIMARY LIFE-SAVING RULE: Safe mechanical lifting
SECONARY LIFE-SAVING RULE: Line of fire
NARRATIVE:
At about 02:21hrs, while rig crew was picking 4” drill pipe, a single drill pipe was picked from Catwalk to the rig
floor with Air winch tugger. The IP removed thread protector from the single pipe while another floorman attempted
to guide the pipe into the mouse hole. The pipe missed the mouse hole, hit the rig floor and also hit the IP on his
right ear and shoulder. IP was move to Clinic.
WHAT WENT WRONG:
1. Lowering without signal – The air tugger operator lowered the pipe without receiving a stop/lower command, due
to absence of a dedicated signaller and reliance on previous experience racking 11 stands without one.
2. Obstructed line of sight – The operator was blindsided by the position of already-racked pipes, limiting visibility of
the mousehole area.
3. IP in fall zone – The injured person was inadvertently in the trajectory of the falling pipe after removing the thread
protector.
4. Incoherent communication – The floormen recognized the pipe had missed the mousehole but were only able to
shout warnings, which were not effectively received
CORRECTIVE ACTIONS AND RECOMMENDATIONS:
1. Updating and endorsing the racking SOP.
2. Assigning a dedicated signaller for all pipe-handling operations.
3. Adjusting derrick camera positioning to restore clear line of sight.
4. Reinforcing communication protocols and hazard-zone controls.
CAUSAL FACTORS:
PEOPLE (ACTS): Following Procedures: Improper position (in the line of fire)
PEOPLE (ACTS): Use of Tools, Equipment, Materials and Products: Improper use/position of tools/equipment/
materials/products
PEOPLE (ACTS): Use of Protective Methods: Failure to warn of hazard
PROCESS (CONDITIONS): Organizational: Inadequate communication

DATE: 08 Oct 2025
COUNTRY: Nigeria
FUNCTION: Production
CAUSE: Struck by (not dropped object)
ACTIVITY: Transport - Land
PRIMARY LIFE-SAVING RULE: Driving
SECONARY LIFE-SAVING RULE: Line of fire
NARRATIVE:
At about 10:30 hours, a company-owned light vehicle in a security convoy travelling veered off the road and collided
with an electric pole. The driver and accompanying customer were safely evacuated and transported to the Clinic for
appropriate medical evaluation / attention.
WHAT WENT WRONG:
1. Driver lost situational awareness and became mentally disengaged (“lost in thought”).
2. Faulty vehicle radio created a quiet environment with no auditory stimulation to help maintain alertness.
3. Vehicle drifted off the road, and driver reaction was delayed.
CORRECTIVE ACTIONS AND RECOMMENDATIONS:
1. Effective vehicle safety systems, such as airbags, seatbelts and prompt emergence response minimizes injury
severity.
2. Driver to always drive maintaining situational awareness.
CAUSAL FACTORS:
PEOPLE (ACTS): Following Procedures: Improper position (in the line of fire)
PEOPLE (ACTS): Inattention/Lack of Awareness: Lack of attention/distracted by other concerns/stress

original_report:
DATE: 03 Jun 2025
COUNTRY: Nigeria
FUNCTION: Construction
CAUSE: Exposure electrical
ACTIVITY: Excavation, trenching, ground disturbance
PRIMARY LIFE-SAVING RULE: Energy isolation
SECONARY LIFE-SAVING RULE: Line of fire
NARRATIVE:
On 3rd June 2025, at about 2:15pm, during a test digging on a 6" test line right of way, the excavator bucket made
contact with a buried 11KVA composite electrical cable. The incident resulted in a dent/superficial cut on the cable.
WHAT WENT WRONG:
1. The excavator was used to accelerate exposure of an underground pipeline despite the presence of multiple
buried utilities.
2. The as-built survey lacked sufficient detail, particularly regarding test line depth and exact routing, leading to
misinterpretation of subsurface conditions.

3. During test digging, the excavator bucket contacted a buried 11 kVA composite electrical cable, causing a dent
and minor cut.
4. Excavator use in close proximity to unidentified/poorly defined underground assets introduced a line-strike
hazard.
CORRECTIVE ACTIONS AND RECOMMENDATIONS:
1. Mechanical excavation (excavators) must not be used near unknown or insufficiently verified buried utilities.
2. Probing results identifying multiple underground facilities must trigger manual excavation only.
3. As-built drawings must be accurate, up-to-date, and detailed, especially regarding depth and horizontal spacing.
4. When indications are unclear, stop work and escalate for engineering verification.
CAUSAL FACTORS:

energy isolation

original_report:
DATE: 18 Feb 2025
COUNTRY: Congo
FUNCTION: Production
CAUSE: Dropped objects
ACTIVITY: Production operations
PRIMARY LIFE-SAVING RULE: Line of fire
SECONARY LIFE-SAVING RULE: Work authorization
NARRATIVE:
A 9 kg metal plate detached from the conveyor railway and fell approximately 6.5–10 m onto the deck below.
No personnel were struck; however, dropped-object energy indicated fatality potential.
The plate was originally installed as a dropped-object prevention measure. Over time it deteriorated and was
displaced due to a misaligned and stretched conveyor belt, which pushed the plate out of position.
Operations on the starboard conveyor were stopped, the area below was barricaded, and a rope-access inspection
of similar installations was initiated.
WHAT WENT WRONG:
• Dropped-object protection plate was not adequately inspected or maintained over time.
• Conveyor belt was poorly fitted/misaligned, creating continuous mechanical load on the plate.
• No inspection programme identified deterioration or displacement risk.Safety-critical equipment (secondary
retention / guarding) was not recognised as such and therefore not verified.
• Asset integrity management and preventative maintenance were ineffective.
CORRECTIVE ACTIONS AND RECOMMENDATIONS:
• Treat dropped-object prevention devices (guards, covers, retention plates) as safety-critical equipment requiring
routine inspection.
• Implement a formal inspection and maintenance programme for conveyors and associated guards.
• Correct belt alignment and tension to prevent abnormal loads on structures.
• Periodically survey elevated plant for dropped-object hazards (e.g., DROPS inspections/rope access).
• Ensure barricading/red-zone control beneath overhead equipment during operations where deterioration is
possible.
CAUSAL FACTORS:
PEOPLE (ACTS): Following Procedures: Improper position (in the line of fire)
PEOPLE (ACTS): Use of Protective Methods: Equipment or materials not secured

PROCESS (CONDITIONS): Tools, Equipment, Materials and Products: Inadequate maintenance/inspection/testing
PROCESS (CONDITIONS): Organizational: Inadequate hazard identification or risk assessment

original_report:
DATE: 23 Mar 2025
COUNTRY: Equatorial Guinea
FUNCTION: Production
CAUSE: Falls from height
ACTIVITY: Lifting, crane, rigging, deck operations
PRIMARY LIFE-SAVING RULE: Line of fire
SECONARY LIFE-SAVING RULE: Safe mechanical lifting
NARRATIVE:
At approximately 06:30, lifting operations were being conducted to move spools from the main deck to the cellar/
sub-cellar deck.
Because no direct lifting path existed, the crew chose to lift the load through a slickline hatch, which constituted
a complex lift and was not covered by the approved PTW. The crane operator had no line of sight and was
communicating by radio only.
During lifting, the hook snagged the hatch plate. The rigger, who was standing on the hatch cover to guide the load,
attempted to stop the lift. The plate dislodged and the rigger fell approximately 6.5 m to the deck below.
The injured person was medevaced with serious injuries. The event had clear fatality potential.
WHAT WENT WRONG:
• A complex lifting operation was performed under a PTW that only authorised a standard lift.
• Work scope changed without risk assessment or lift planning.
• Crane operator had no line of sight and communications were unreliable.
• Rigger stood on the hatch cover to guide the load, placing himself in a fall hazard zone.
• The lift was coordinated using voice/radio in a noisy area without clear signalling control.
• Rigger’s certification had expired and supervision was inadequate.
• Unsafe practice had become normalised due to prior similar lifts performed without incident.
CORRECTIVE ACTIONS AND RECOMMENDATIONS:
• Complex lifts require a specific lift plan, risk assessment, and supervision.
• Never route loads through hatches/openings without engineered lifting arrangements.
• Maintain line of sight or use a designated trained signalman with agreed communication protocol.
• Personnel must never stand on removable covers or under suspended loads.
• Verify competency and certification of riggers and lifting personnel.
• Stop work when lift conditions differ from the approved plan.
CAUSAL FACTORS:

PROCESS (CONDITIONS): Work Place Hazards: Congestion, clutter or restricted motion

NARRATIVE:
While parking the starboard (STBD) crane following routine lifting operations, the crane boom was brought down
into the boom rest abruptly rather than in a controlled manner. This sudden placement generated an unexpected
impact load on the crane structure, producing a loud bang that was heard in the vicinity of the crane pedestal and
surrounding areas.
The abrupt motion and resulting impact load may have introduced a shock event into the crane’s hydraulic or
electrical systems. A process shutdown occurred minutes after this impact, and although the causal link has not yet
been fully established, the timing suggests the crane event may have contributed to or triggered the shutdown.
WHAT WENT WRONG:
• Crane boom impacted boom rest heavily.
• Crane incorrectly lowered at the boom rest.
• Lack of experience of Crane Operator.
CORRECTIVE ACTIONS AND RECOMMENDATIONS:
1. Mandatory contractor equipment specific training familiarization to be performed onboard and documented with
new crane operators.
2. Selection of candidates for temporary cover to be formalized with the minimum experience requirement for
contractor operations
3. New crane operators to be mobilized in advance to come offshore and undergo supervision monitored by the
facility crane operator for a defined supervision period.
4. Non-destructive testing to be performed at the crane's boom & cradle by 3rd party.

NARRATIVE:
Contractor carrying out repairs on the Scale Inhibitor Injection system, the system was understood to have been
depressurised. As the contractor started to release an end cap, the cap was projected downwards under pressure.
The cap went directly downwards into a section of plant close to a walkway. This could have had potential to impact
personnel.
WHAT WENT WRONG:
Failure to properly depressurise closed circuit.
CORRECTIVE ACTIONS AND RECOMMENDATIONS:
Learning 1. The process for managing valve movements during a leak test in response to a leak was not robust. The
leak testing procedure was not explicit about how to manage such a situation. Also no bridging document between
procedure and company Control of Work procedure.
Learning 2. Site team did not verify that the leak test system envelope was fully depressurised. Task fatigue and
normalisation of the risk were identified resulting in the Permit Authority deciding to de-prioritise some oversight of
the task.
Learning 3. The potential hazard created using 6Mo tubing and 316 stainless steel fittings at tubing geometries
outside of manufacturer recommendation was not understood. Knowing this may have influenced decisions around
controls such as exclusion zones and proving zero energy at the point of system being worked on.

FUNCTION: Production
CAUSE: Dropped objects
ACTIVITY: Office, warehouse, accommodation, catering
PRIMARY LIFE-SAVING RULE: Safe mechanical lifting
SECONARY LIFE-SAVING RULE: Line of fire
NARRATIVE:
During pallet racking activities in the warehouse, a forklift was in the process of lifting a pallet to the third shelf. The
load backrest of the forklift inadvertently contacted another pallet directly above (load approximately 240kg) stored
on the fourth shelf which dislodged and fell approximately 5.6m to grade. No personnel were injured. There was one
nearby person 7 meters away.
WHAT WENT WRONG:
Incompatibility between the forklift (material handling equipment) in use and the racking system configuration
installed. The distance between shelf three and shelf four was 1350mm. The height of the forklift backrest was
1250mm. This left 100mm between the two and when manoeuvring the load into position resulted in the load above
being lifted inadvertently. The higher you lift the forklift mast, the more important adequate clearances become.
CORRECTIVE ACTIONS AND RECOMMENDATIONS:
Equipment Compatibility Must Be Verified - Ensure all material handling equipment and load types are assessed for
compatibility with racking systems before use or when managing change. This includes verifying dimensions and
manoeuvrability.
Critical Importance of Adequate Clearance - Maintain safe clearance margins between shelving levels, loads and
the material handling equipment, especially when operating at height.
CAUSAL FACTORS:
PEOPLE (ACTS): Following Procedures: Improper position (in the line of fire)

of change

FUNCTION: Production
CAUSE: Pressure release
ACTIVITY: Maintenance, inspection, testing
PRIMARY LIFE-SAVING RULE: Energy isolation
SECONARY LIFE-SAVING RULE: Line of fire
NARRATIVE:
IP1 observed visible bulging of a drain hose and proceeded to disconnect it. Although the associated compressor
had been isolated, the hose remained connected to the main drainage manifold, which was linked to 24
compressors.
The hose remained pressurized, and upon disconnection it struck the IP1 on the left hand and lower leg, and
subsequently impacting IP2’s hand as they attempted to assist. As a result, IP1 and IP2 were injured.
WHAT WENT WRONG:
The task continued despite incomplete isolation: only the compressor was isolated while the hose remained
connected to a pressurized shared manifold, the hose’s visible bulging signalled residual pressure, and the plan
was informally changed without a full risk assessment.
CORRECTIVE ACTIONS AND RECOMMENDATIONS:
Recognize and respond to deviations, verify isolation across the entire system, and avoid informal adaptations -
promote a disciplined “Stop and Verify” culture that empowers pausing and reassessment when conditions change.

NARRATIVE:
A crew member stepped out of a cherry picker while connecting a hydraulic hose to the Annular BOP, lost balance,
and fell onto the cellar-pit grating. Subsequent hospital evaluation confirmed a left zygomatic bone fracture.
WHAT WENT WRONG:
Proper access was not planned, leading the worker to step out of the cherry picker without fall protection, bypassing
a critical safety control and exposing him to an unprotected fall hazard.

be planned and used to eliminate the temptation to step out of equipment and expose workers to unprotected fall
hazards.
